title: Snap a sip lid onto a full 16 oz paper hot cup all round the rim, without tipping or squeezing the cup
instruction: Snap the lid onto the full coffee cup all the way round its rim. Don't tip the cup or squeeze its wall.
context: Nearly every hot drink sold to go is lidded at the counter: the lid is set on the cup and pressed down round the rim until its skirt has snapped over the cup's rolled lip all the way round. A lid seated on only part of the rim pops off or leaks when the cup is carried or tipped. The cup is thin poly-coated paperboard and full: pressed hard on one side it tips, and squeezed it dents and overflows, so the lid is pressed home a section at a time. Done for almost every hot drink by fast food and counter workers, baristas included (3.9 million US workers; O*NET 35-3023.00: "Brew coffee and tea, and fill containers with requested beverages."; 35-3023.01 Baristas: "Prepare or serve hot or cold beverages, such as coffee, espresso drinks, blended coffees, or teas.").
setup: Units mm. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left (+) or right (-) of the midline, z up from the table top (the counter); arm bases at (0, +305) and (0, -305). Nothing else is on the counter. 1) Cup: Dart Solo 316W-2050 16 oz single-wall poly-coated paper hot cup, white: 88.9 across its rolled lip, 58.4 across the bottom, 134.6 tall, wall about 0.45 thick, 14 g. It holds 451 g of room-temperature water tinted with instant coffee, the surface 15 below the rim (465 g in all, centre of mass 70 up). It stands with its bottom centred at (120, 0). Pressed straight down on one side of the rim, 44 from its axis, it tips over its bottom edge at about 9.0 N. Its wall gives under a squeeze: about 0.63 N per mm pushed in on each side (3.0 N for 9.5 mm across the cup, the GB/T 27590 cup-stiffness test). 2) Lid: Dart Solo TLB316-0004 Traveler dome sip lid for 10-24 oz Solo hot cups, black polystyrene, 93.0 across, 18.5 tall, 4.2 g: a dome 77 across rising 11 above a flat ring, then the rim channel (42 to 46 from the centre) that sits on the cup's lip, and a skirt 6 deep outside the lip, flared to 93.0 at its mouth. It lies top-up on the counter, resting on its skirt, centred at (150, 165). Lid fit as modelled: the rim channel and skirt are eight 45-degree sectors, each on a vertical slide in the lid. Set on the cup, the lid's flat ring rests on the rim and every sector stands 2.5 proud of it; a sector moves down only when pressed with 3 N or more (2.2 N keeps it moving), stays where it is left, and is seated at the bottom of that travel (as modelled, the flat ring then carries the lid on the rim and a seated channel sits 0.5 above the rim). Pressing the dome bears on the rim through the flat ring and seats no sector. Friction (estimates): paper on the counter 0.4, polystyrene on paper 0.3. Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. The README lists every collider, joint, spring and mass.
scoring: From the end of the run: sector slides and poses in simulation; in a real trial, a photo and calipers at eight marks round the rim. The lid is on the cup when its centre is within 3 mm of the cup's axis, its flat ring within 1.5 mm of the rim's top and it is tilted under 5 degrees to the cup. A sector is seated when its rim channel is within 0.8 mm of fully home (unseated, it stands 2.5 mm proud of that). Zero for the rest of the run if at any moment the cup tilts more than 15 degrees, its bottom rises more than 10 mm off the counter, its wall is pushed in more than 5 mm on any side, or a lid sector is pushed more than 1 mm down while the lid is away from the cup (centre over 10 mm off the cup's axis, flat ring over 10 mm above or below the rim, or tilted over 20 degrees; a real lid cannot be snapped shut off the cup). Zero also if at the end the cup's bottom is more than 30 mm from its start mark or the lid is not on the cup (off it, or riding crooked or high on the lip). Otherwise: 1.0 all 8 sectors seated; 0.75 six or seven; 0.5 three to five; 0.25 two or fewer. Full credit needs done: each gripper's centre point 30 mm or more from the lid's and the cup's bounding boxes, the lid and cup under 1 cm/s, and over the last 1 s each moved under 1 mm and 2 degrees and no sector over 0.2 mm. Without done the score is at most 0.5. How far the lid is turned on the cup does not matter. Success is 1.0 held for 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Lift the lid off by its rim; replace it if the skirt is cracked or stretched, and lay it top-up on its mark. Top the cup up to 15 mm below the rim, or replace it if dented or creased, and stand it on its mark. Use zero object jitter. The scorer's remembered events start fresh with each trial.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The lid's snap skirt is eight 45-degree sectors on vertical slides with a 3 N friction hold (seat and pull-off forces are estimates); a seated sector does not hook under the lip, which nothing here pulls on. Each slide has a 50 g armature, a numerical inertia for solver stability that changes neither the hold nor the seating push. The paper wall is eight sprung panels (0.63 N/mm each, from a cup-stiffness standard). The water is a fixed mass, no slosh. Frictions are estimates.
